# Element reference

Every Abaqus element type the converter recognises, its node count, and how it is emitted for CalculiX. **Substitutions preserve the node count** so connectivity stays valid. Solid/shell node *ordering* is identical between the two codes, so connectivity is passed through unchanged. A substitution is exact only where noted; any other replaces Abaqus' element formulation, which the converter records as reduced physics (`Converter.reduced_physics`, a header warning): ccx then solves a different discretization than Abaqus.

Direct CalculiX types: **68**. Total recognised: **175**.

| `T3D3` | 3 | direct |

Every 3-node beam runs as ccx's `B32R`, the 20-node brick integrated at 2 × 2 × 2 points: 2 along the beam, as Abaqus integrates its quadratic beams (`B22`, `B32`, `PIPE22`, `PIPE32`). ccx's `B32` integrates at 3 × 3 × 3 and locks on coarse meshes (a cantilever's tip deflection under an end load: 0.77 of beam theory on one element, 0.95 on two; exact on any number of `B32R`).

Under a `*BEAM SECTION, SECTION=CIRC`, `PIPE`, `BOX` or `THICK PIPE` (emitted as `PIPE`), 2-node beams whose emitted type is `B21` → `B32R`, `B31` → `B32R`, `B31R` → `B32R` become 3-node beams: ccx 2.23 rejects linear beams with a circular section and runs `PIPE` and `BOX` sections only on `B32R`. Each element gets a new midside node at the midpoint of its end nodes (ccx's order is end, middle, end); element ids and sets are kept, and BCs, temperatures and initial conditions given for both end nodes also reach the midside node. The 3-node beam is a different element than Abaqus' 2-node one, so such a deck counts as reduced physics.

ccx has no planar beam or truss — it runs `B21` as `B31` and `T2D2` as `T3D2` — so the out-of-plane DOFs of `B21`, `B22`, `B23`, `PIPE21`, `PIPE22`, `T2D2`, `T2D3` (and their `H`/`T` variants) are free in ccx. In a planar model (no 3-D elements, all their nodes at one z) the converter fixes DOF 3 on their nodes, midside nodes included (node set `ABQ2CCX_PLANAR`, model data, repeated after `*BOUNDARY, OP=NEW`), and DOFs 4-5 at one node of a straight beam whose twist nothing restrains (on a circular section, an element's middle node: at an end node ccx 2.23 would lock the bending rotation too). The rotations are not fixed on every node (that stiffens ccx's expanded beams), so `*FREQUENCY` results include twist modes that Abaqus' planar beams do not have (warned).

Beams under a section only ccx's `U1` element carries (`*BEAM GENERAL SECTION`, `SECTION=I`) — `B21`, `B21H`, `B23`, `B23H`, `B31`, `B31H`, `B33`, `B33H` — are written as `U1`, all of the deck's or none (see the keyword reference). `U1` is a cubic Euler–Bernoulli beam: exact for `B23`/`B33` in statics; the shear-flexible ones lose their shear deformation, and its mass matrix differs from Abaqus' cubic beams' (reduced physics). In a 2-D model DOFs 3–5 are held at every `U1` node.

ccx 2.23 expands every membrane element into a solid on nodes of its own and leaves the mid-thickness node of a quadratic element's corners free (`M3D8R` singular, `M3D6` and `M3D8` too soft). The converter writes those solids itself: per element and node a bottom and a top node held at the membrane node by `*EQUATION` (bottom + top = 2 × node), per corner node a mid-thickness node equal to it, per `C3D20R` one equation that holds its zero-energy hourglass; loads, faces and sets stay the membrane's (`validate_with_ccx.py quad_membrane_*`).

## plane stress

| Abaqus type | Nodes | CalculiX |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CPS3` | 3 | direct |
| `CPS4` | 4 | direct |
| `CPS4I` | 4 | → `C3D8I` slab (exact for small-strain linear elasticity in static steps); otherwise → `CPS4`, reduced physics |
| `CPS4R` | 4 | direct |
| `CPS6` | 6 | direct |
| `CPS6M` | 6 | → `CPS6` (substituted: reduced physics) |
| `CPS8` | 8 | direct |
| `CPS8R` | 8 | direct |

ccx has no incompatible-mode plane element. `CPS4I` and `CPE4I` (the latter on parallelograms: Abaqus adds a fifth, volumetric mode that acts only on distorted elements) become one-element-thick `C3D8I` slabs: the 2-D nodes are the bottom face (ids, BCs and loads kept), new top nodes one section thickness above follow their in-plane DOFs by `*EQUATION`, and DOF 3 of every slab node is held (node set `ABQ2CCX_SLAB`, repeated after `*BOUNDARY, OP=NEW`), so the slab deforms in plane strain and the C3D8I's modes are those of Abaqus' four-mode element. `CPS4I` gets the plane-stress stiffness as an `ORTHO` material with no coupling to the thickness direction, so S33 = 0. Probed on 2.23 against a 2-D implementation of the incompatible-mode element (rectangular and skewed meshes): equal to 1e-7; `validate_with_ccx.py cps4i_slab` checks pure bending against beam theory. Outside small-strain linear elasticity in static steps (`NLGEOM`, other materials, contact, couplings, `*FREQUENCY` / `*BUCKLE`, whose mass and geometric stiffness are not compared ...) the element runs as `CPS4`/`CPE4`, which locks in bending, and counts as reduced physics.

## rigid

| Abaqus type | Nodes | CalculiX |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `R2D2` | 2 | → `C3D8` skin through the model's thickness, 3-D rigid body held in the plane (exact; `S5` / `S3`) |
| `R3D3` | 3 | → `C3D6` skin of its rigid body (exact; face `S2` = `SPOS`, `S1` = `SNEG`) |
| `R3D4` | 4 | → `C3D8` skin of its rigid body (exact; face `S2` = `SPOS`, `S1` = `SNEG`) |
| `RAX2` | 2 | → `C3D8` skin over ccx's ±1° sector, 3-D rigid body held in the plane (exact; `S5` / `S3`) |
| `RB2D2` | 2 | → `C3D8` skin through the model's thickness, 3-D rigid body held in the plane (exact; `S5` / `S3`) |
| `RB3D2` | 2 | not emitted — its nodes join its rigid body |

ccx has no rigid element, and its `*RIGID BODY` refuses shell/beam nodes, so each rigid element becomes a force-free solid *skin* that its rigid body carries (element set and material `ABQ2CCX_RIGID`): one face is the element itself, pointing along its `SPOS` normal (the right-hand rule over the nodes; 2-D: node 1 → 2 turned 90° counterclockwise); a `SNEG` side gets the skin on the other side, an unlabelled surface both. The skin moves rigidly, so its material, thickness and density (0; tiny in explicit dynamics) change nothing; its material is written after the deck's own (ccx's default contact stiffness comes from the first material). Plane and axisymmetric skins are 3-D bricks across ccx's expansion of the 2-D model under a 3-D body: ccx's 2-D rigid body follows its expansion only linearly under `NLGEOM` rotation and reports no reaction with face-to-face contact. Analytical rigid surfaces (`*SURFACE, TYPE=SEGMENTS / CYLINDER / REVOLUTION`) are meshed into the same skins — see the keyword reference.

ccx 2.23 runs a composite `*SHELL SECTION` on `S6` and `S8R` only, and has no layered solid section. Linear composite shells become `S6`/`S8R` with a node at the middle of every edge, shared with the linear shells and 2-node beams joined to them by an edge, which are upgraded too. Composite continuum shells become one solid per ply, stacked from the bottom face (`STACK DIRECTION`), each its share of the thickness with its material and ply axes; sets, faces, face loads, BCs and node sets follow the plies. Both are validated against classical lamination theory and Pagano's 3-D solution (`validate_with_ccx.py composite_plate_*`).

## surface (load carrier)

| Abaqus type | Nodes | CalculiX |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SFM3D3` | 3 | left out of the mesh; its loads → consistent nodal forces |
| `SFM3D4` | 4 | left out of the mesh; its loads → consistent nodal forces |
| `SFM3D4R` | 4 | left out of the mesh; its loads → consistent nodal forces |
| `SFM3D6` | 6 | left out of the mesh; its loads → consistent nodal forces |
| `SFM3D8` | 8 | left out of the mesh; its loads → consistent nodal forces |
| `SFM3D8R` | 8 | left out of the mesh; its loads → consistent nodal forces |
| `SFMAX1` | 2 | left out of the mesh; its loads → consistent nodal forces |
| `SFMAX2` | 3 | left out of the mesh; its loads → consistent nodal forces |
| `SFMGAX1` | 2 | left out of the mesh; its loads → consistent nodal forces |
| `SFMGAX2` | 3 | left out of the mesh; its loads → consistent nodal forces |

Abaqus surface elements have no stiffness ("membrane elements with zero thickness") and ccx has none, so they leave the mesh: element sets keep their other members, and the `TRVEC`, `TRSHR` and `P` loads they carry (element-based, or `*DSLOAD` on their `SPOS`/`SNEG` side) become consistent nodal forces on their nodes — the 3-D ones as faces (corners, then midside nodes), the axisymmetric ones as edges (end, middle, end; over the full circle). Abaqus signs: an element-based `P` acts along the element normal (right-hand rule over the nodes; axisymmetric: node 1 → 2 turned counterclockwise), a surface `P` against the surface normal. Elements that carry `*REBAR LAYER`s, or mass (`*SURFACE SECTION, DENSITY=`) in a dynamic or frequency step or under gravity, stay — ccx then stops on them — unless `--approximate`.
